title: cred-spec PR #50 — vetting as a statement predicate: say why its identity commitment is not the ADR-001 voucher linkage
what: #49 closed 09-13 in favour of #50 (stormer78, builds on #47). The profile's identityCommitment is a per-application salted digest of the applicant's identity CLAIMS, recomputable by every vetter so a community can see that several statements concern one claimed identity. That is a commitment to claims for an admission decision — it neither opens to a holder secret (007/004) nor sits in a membership root (001), so it cannot stand in for the voucher's VMC-side linkage that 010 clause 4 needs, and a proof over it establishes nothing about membership or key control. Where it does land: record 008 route 1 (a salted commitment opened against a context the verifier holds), with the profile's own retention caveat — a vetter who keeps a card can recognise the commitment later. Mitch's 13 September review (~/Documents/Codex/2026-09-07/rev/outputs/2026-09-13-vetting-linkage-review.md) is folded in: its candidate wording sits in the Implementation Guide (step 5) and the Research and Book chapter; its response candidate is draft W (ledger 37); record 010 carries the negative-space line and three fixture requirements as codes without vectors.
